items.title: GAKPO AND ISAK LOOK LIKE GREAT FPL PICKS  ⚽️ FUL (H) in GW4 👀  @FPLRaptor #fpl #premierleague
items.headline: Isak and Gakpo emerge as Liverpool’s best Fulham punts in Gameweek 4
items.summary:
Liverpool’s home match against Fulham in Gameweek 4 stands out as one of the strongest alternatives to the Chelsea-Haaland fixture. Fulham concede heavily early in the season and are viewed as one of the league’s weakest defences, making this an attractive one-week entry point for Liverpool attackers.

Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo are preferred over Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz on both the eye test and underlying data. Liverpool are expected to keep creating high-quality chances under Andoni Iraola’s attacking approach, as his Bournemouth teams do, but Isak and Gakpo currently look like the most convincing routes into those chances. Gakpo appears relatively secure for minutes, while Isak is the standout target for managers buying now or activating a Wildcard.

The main caution is Liverpool’s fixture swing immediately after Fulham. Their run includes Bournemouth, Manchester City, Brentford, Brighton and Arsenal, with Arsenal leading the league for expected goals conceded, City second and Brentford also posting strong defensive numbers. Brighton looks a potentially exploitable fixture, but the overall schedule is not strong enough to make Liverpool attackers automatic long-term holds.

Managers who already own Szoboszlai may reasonably keep him, particularly because of his reliable minutes and possible penalty involvement, rather than using a transfer or chip to chase another Liverpool option. For new buyers, however, Gameweek 4 is the time to act: Isak is the preferred signing, Gakpo is a viable alternative, and managers who pass on Liverpool this week may be better served looking elsewhere unless they are building a Haaland-free squad.
key_points: Liverpool at home to Fulham in Gameweek 4 is a prime attacking fixture because Fulham are among the weakest defences so far.
Alexander Isak is the preferred Liverpool buy for managers making a transfer or playing a Wildcard.
Cody Gakpo is also an appealing option, with strong recent performances and relatively secure minutes.
Dominik Szoboszlai remains a reasonable hold for current owners due to his minutes and potential penalty duty.
Liverpool’s fixtures worsen after Fulham, with Manchester City, Brentford and Arsenal all presenting difficult defensive opposition.
Managers buying a Liverpool attacker should view Gameweek 4 as the key entry point rather than a long-term fixture run.

items.title: GW4 vs GW6 WILDCARD FOR FPL? 🍟 📝 @FPLRaptor  #fpl #premierleague #football #wildcard
items.headline: Gameweek 6 Wildcard remains the plan despite Gameweek 4 team-value pressure
items.summary:
The current preference is to save the Wildcard until Gameweek 6 rather than join the popular Gameweek 3 or 4 activation. Three early transfers have already been made for Gameweek 4, bringing in Pal Dardai, Mehammed Besic and Morgan Gibbs-White, with all three viewed as useful short-term picks ahead of the international break.

Gameweek 4 has appeal because the three-week international break creates uncertainty: injuries, rotation and changing form can quickly reshape squads, while a Wildcard restores flexibility through extra transfers. It also offers a route to increase exposure to Arsenal and Chelsea, two sides worth targeting but not currently owned heavily. Activating early could improve the immediate squad and help recover ground in team value.

However, Gameweek 4 is not considered an especially strong fixture-swing point, and the existing squad is already built to perform through Gameweeks 4 and 5. The downside of waiting is lower team value than managers who have already Wildcarded, but the benefit is more information before committing to a new structure. Unless a key player is injured or another major issue emerges in midweek, the plan is to resist the short-term value gain and hold the Wildcard for Gameweek 6.
key_points: The preferred Wildcard timing is Gameweek 6, not Gameweek 4, because the present squad is still well set for Gameweeks 4 and 5.
Pal Dardai, Mehammed Besic and Morgan Gibbs-White arrive as three early Gameweek 4 transfers for short-term value.
A Gameweek 4 Wildcard would allow increased investment in Arsenal and Chelsea, who are currently underrepresented in the squad.
The international break makes Gameweek 4 an attractive contingency Wildcard window because injuries and rotation can change plans quickly.
Lower team value is accepted as the cost of waiting, with extra information viewed as more valuable than chasing price rises.
A key midweek injury or other major squad problem could still trigger a Gameweek 4 Wildcard.

items.title: FPL GW4 Transfer Tips 🔥 SELL Bruno ❌ Palmer IN ✅
items.headline: Cole Palmer edges Morgan Rogers as Chelsea’s key Gameweek 4 target
items.summary:
Chelsea attack is the main Gameweek 4 target as Hull visit Stamford Bridge. Hull have started with three clean sheets, but that is too small a sample to conclude they are difficult to break down, while Chelsea have scored early in every match and look strong going forward. Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are all viable additions, with Chelsea’s wider run also appealing: after Hull, they have Bournemouth, Spurs, Manchester United, Sunderland, Leeds and Crystal Palace, predominantly at home. That makes Chelsea players easier to hold through less attractive fixtures rather than forcing an immediate exit plan.

João Pedro remains the standout value forward at £7.7m, with 90-minute appearances in every match and ownership above 72%, but he is not considered essential if squad structure requires spending elsewhere. Between Palmer and Rogers, the deciding factor is captaincy. Palmer’s previous output, apparent penalty responsibility and higher ceiling make him the preferred captain in Chelsea’s home fixtures, notably Gameweeks 4, 6 and 8. Rogers is a strong cheaper alternative, particularly for managers retaining Bruno Fernandes; Fernandes plus Rogers is judged slightly preferable to Palmer plus Bryan Mbeumo. Any pair of the three Chelsea options works, but Palmer and João Pedro is the preferred combination.

Liverpool assets are holds rather than buys before Fulham at home. Mohamed Salah remains worth keeping because of penalties, set pieces, guaranteed minutes and multiple routes to points, even if his open-play threat can make ownership frustrating. Florian Wirtz is also worth holding for Fulham if already owned, but his falling price and lack of returns mean he is not a transfer target. Alexander Isak’s two-goal haul against Ipswich has created excessive hype: at £9.1m, he lacks penalties, is vulnerable to early substitutions once Champions League football begins and may require two transfers to acquire. He is a fine short-term option but not a priority over Bukayo Saka, who offers set pieces and penalty potential. Liverpool’s tougher upcoming stretch—Bournemouth away, Manchester City, Brentford away, Brighton and Arsenal—limits the appeal of new double or triple attack investment.

Arsenal’s defensive dominance makes two defenders the preferred minimum on a Wildcard, with triple defence still attractive. Martin Ødegaard at £6.6m is nevertheless a compelling alternative to Saka for managers who do not expect to captain Arsenal often; he is starting regularly, linking well with Kai Havertz and collecting bonus when he returns. Saka remains the superior Arsenal captain due to penalties, but Arsenal’s most obvious captaincy week is Hull at home in Gameweek 10, so Ødegaard’s value can outweigh that premium. Dominic Calvert-Lewin should be held for Newcastle and Crystal Palace at home, while Everton’s Thierno Barry is the standout cheap-forward target after Beto’s departure leaves him with improved minutes, possible penalties and a good run from Gameweek 5. Yoane Wissa is also a hold through Leeds, Hull and Coventry despite occasionally operating deeper, as his minutes and possible penalty role remain valuable.
key_points: Target Chelsea against Hull in Gameweek 4, with Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers all strong options for a favourable largely home-heavy fixture run.
Palmer is preferred over Rogers for managers wanting a reliable alternative captain, while João Pedro remains excellent value but is not compulsory at 72% ownership.
Hold Salah and Wirtz for Fulham at home if already owned, but avoid rushing into Liverpool attackers ahead of a tougher run beginning at Bournemouth away.
Do not chase Isak solely after his Ipswich haul: his £9.1m price, lack of penalties and possible Champions League minute management weaken his long-term appeal.
On a Gameweek 4 Wildcard, prioritise at least two Arsenal defenders; Ødegaard is a credible £6.6m attacking alternative if Saka captaincy is not central to the plan.
Keep Calvert-Lewin for home matches against Newcastle and Crystal Palace, as he has penalties, strong underlying chances and regular 90-minute potential.
Barry becomes a leading budget forward at £5.6m after Everton sell Beto without replacing him; he has improved security of starts and may inherit penalties.
Keep Wissa through Gameweek 6 rather than reacting to his deeper spells, with Leeds away, Hull at home and Coventry away still a useful run.

items.title: FPL GW4 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 4 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: João Pedro and Chelsea’s attack top the Gameweek 4 transfer agenda
items.summary:
João Pedro is the standout buy and a clear hold for Gameweek 4, with Chelsea hosting Hull before favourable matches against Bournemouth and Everton. Hull’s consecutive clean sheets mask poor defensive underlying numbers and weak opposition, while Chelsea’s attack has looked strong outside the Arsenal match. Cole Palmer is the premium midfield priority because he combines high shot volume with penalties and set pieces; Morgan Rogers is also attractive for his shooting and creativity, although a triple Chelsea attack carries some concentration risk. Erling Haaland remains a hold and a viable captain away to Manchester United, with Sunderland and Ipswich at home among Manchester City’s next four fixtures.

Liverpool assets also merit patience for Fulham at home. Mohamed Salah remains a non-negotiable hold despite recent sales, having come close to returns and retaining penalties, set pieces and open-play threat against a Fulham side that is vulnerable defensively. Alexander Isak is worth holding for Fulham, but is not worth major squad reconstruction after his two-goal haul against Ipswich, especially with Manchester City and Brentford to follow. Virgil van Dijk is similarly worth one more week for Fulham before becoming expendable. Bruno Fernandes is only a sell if downgrading him funds multiple upgrades; a single-transfer exit ahead of Manchester City is discouraged because Fulham away follows.

Among forwards, Barry at £5.6m and Fulham’s Gonzalo are the preferred medium-term purchases behind João Pedro. Barry is expected to play regularly as Everton’s available central forward, may have penalties and gets Ipswich and Hull in Gameweeks 5 and 6. Gonzalo has played 90 minutes in each match, posts strong shot numbers and potentially takes penalties, while Fulham face Ipswich, Hull and Coventry from Gameweeks 6 to 8. Yoane Wissa is a hold rather than a fresh buy: Newcastle’s chance creation has dipped, his penalty role and central position are less certain after Fernandez Pardo’s arrival, and he may face reduced minutes or a deeper role when Osula returns. Viktor Gyökeres is an urgent sale because he is not starting for Arsenal, while Mateta is injured and Watkins has left the Premier League.

Arsenal’s defence is the clearest route for defensive transfers. Conor is described as an exceptional £4.4m buy with Saliba absent until around Christmas, strong defensive-contribution potential and excellent clean-sheet fixtures against Sunderland, Leeds and Forest. Riccardo Calafiori is also a buy due to his advanced threat, apparent first-choice status and Arsenal’s elite defensive numbers. Leeds defender Maharovic is a cheaper differential with major defensive-contribution output and set-piece upside, though he needs rotating for Arsenal and Manchester United in Gameweeks 6 and 7. Avoid Sunderland defenders because of poor fixtures and rotation concerns, while Manchester City attackers other than Haaland are risky amid Champions League-driven rotation. Harvey Barnes and Elanga are also avoid calls: recent returns substantially exceed weak underlying numbers.
key_points: Captain João Pedro or Cole Palmer for Chelsea’s home match against Hull; Haaland away to Manchester United is the alternative premium captain.
Buy João Pedro immediately if absent, with Hull and Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge offering the strongest short-term fixtures.
Hold Salah for Fulham at home rather than switching to Cody Gakpo, whose long-term minutes become less secure after Liverpool’s new arrivals.
Prioritise Barry or Gonzalo as longer-term forward buys; Wissa is less appealing because Newcastle create little and his role may change.
Sell Gyökeres for lack of starts, Mateta because of injury, Watkins because he has left the Premier League, and Rodon because he is out until late October.
Buy Conor as Arsenal’s £4.4m defensive route while Saliba is sidelined; Calafiori is the higher-upside alternative.
Avoid non-Haaland Manchester City midfielders such as Cherki, Foden and Doku/Anjai because European and cup commitments increase rotation risk.
Keep Gabriel and Raya through Arsenal’s favourable fixture run, while Kinsky is the preferred £4.5m goalkeeper option.

items.headline: Ezre Concer offers cut-price Arsenal clean sheets, but rotation caps his appeal
items.summary:
Ezre Concer strengthens his case as a £4.4m route into Arsenal’s defence after starting in Gameweek 3 and collecting defensive-contribution points. Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential gives him a very high floor for his price, making him particularly attractive for managers using a Wildcard.

The main concern is security of starts. Mosca is absent from the squad, and his return to fitness could alter Concer’s place in the side. Arsenal also face Champions League commitments alongside Premier League matches, so fixture congestion increases the risk of rotation in defence.

There is also an opportunity-cost question over Arsenal’s three-player limit. Concer is far cheaper than Gabriel and David Raya, but selecting him as part of a defensive double-up or triple-up could prevent managers from buying Arsenal attackers. Solace has another assist, Odigard scores, and Bay Saka starts the season well, leaving several competing options for Arsenal slots.

Concer’s ceiling remains the reason not to treat him as an automatic buy. He has limited established attacking threat and defensive-contribution returns may not be regular, although his presence in the box against Chelsea offers some encouragement. He is not essential yet, but his price and Arsenal’s defensive strength make him a difficult player to ignore on a Gameweek 4 Wildcard.
key_points: Ezre Concer starts in Gameweek 3 and returns defensive-contribution points, enhancing his appeal at £4.4m.
Arsenal clean sheets give Concer a strong points floor, especially compared with more expensive options such as Gabriel and David Raya.
Mosca’s eventual return and Arsenal’s Champions League schedule create a meaningful rotation risk for Concer.
Concer has limited proven attacking upside, so his ceiling is lower than that of Arsenal’s more attacking defenders or midfielders.
Using Concer occupies an Arsenal squad slot that could otherwise go to Solace, Odigard or Bay Saka.
He is a strong Wildcard selection but is not yet an essential transfer for managers with a settled defence.

items.title: 14 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 4 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Arsenal’s defence leads the GW4 FPL agenda as Cherki and Foden compete for City’s central role
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 arrives with Champions League and Carabao Cup ties still to come, making early transfers riskier than usual despite the temptation to catch price rises. Managers are advised to weigh that risk against any urgent squad issues, particularly with several players carrying uncertain fitness or minutes prospects.

Arsenal’s defensive numbers are the standout early-season FPL story. They have conceded less than 1.0 expected goal across their opening three matches, making their defenders and goalkeeper premium targets, while Zubimendi strengthens his case as a budget midfield option after starting again and completing 90 minutes despite his early Gameweek 2 withdrawal. Honza also makes his first start and registers defensive contributions at £4.4m, offering value if his role holds. By contrast, H has yet to concede an actual goal but has allowed more than 5.0 xG, suggesting that clean-sheet record is vulnerable.

Manchester City’s midfield remains difficult to predict: Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are expected to share central minutes, limiting both as secure starts. Nico O’Reilly suffers an injury in the warm-up against Coventry, although Enzo Maresca says it does not appear serious. Nathan Collins is a clearer concern after leaving with a calf strain and has no return timeline. Mamedu Sangari also shows he is susceptible to early substitutions, albeit after picking up a yellow card.

Liverpool’s attacking shape offers a possible route into their forwards. When Hugo Ekitike is substituted, Cody Gakpo moves through the middle at number nine, a pattern that may continue. Dominik Szoboszlai begins in midfield before moving to right wing after substitutions and nearly wins a penalty, underlining his attacking involvement. Elsewhere, Diper starts on the left again and appears secure until MTO returns, while Inai is likely to continue playing until Dou is fit, though that return could be imminent. At Nottingham Forest, Munos makes his debut with AA dropping out, which should keep Neco Williams nailed for now.
key_points: Delay non-essential Gameweek 4 transfers until after the Champions League and Carabao Cup matches, as midweek rotation and injuries increase the downside of moving early.
Arsenal are the premier defensive target after allowing under 1.0 xG in three matches, while their opponents’ early clean sheets look less sustainable after conceding more than 5.0 xG.
Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are expected to share central Manchester City minutes, reducing the security of either midfield pick.
Nathan Collins has a calf strain with no stated return date, making him an injury watch and a potential transfer out.
Cody Gakpo plays as Liverpool’s number nine after Hugo Ekitike goes off, giving him an additional attacking route despite uncertainty over his starting role.
Dominik Szoboszlai’s move from midfield to right wing late on increases his attacking potential, while he nearly wins a penalty.
Neco Williams looks set to remain Nottingham Forest’s secure option after Munos debuts and AA makes way.
Zubimendi completes 90 minutes for Arsenal and Honza records defensive contributions on his first start at £4.4m, though both remain value picks dependent on sustained minutes.

items.summary:

Palmer is preferred to Morgan Rogers as a short-term explosive option before an intended wildcard in the next couple of weeks, and he is immediately given the captaincy. The other confirmed transfers bring Morgan Gibbs-White into midfield in place of Arsenal’s Sol Bamba, despite Bamba returning again. The concern is Bamba’s security of starts, while Gibbs-White offers a more reliable route to minutes. At the back, injured Leeds defender Rodon is upgraded to teammate Muhamed Besic, who is viewed as a useful depth option with attacking potential and a favourable short-term fixture run.

The side lines up in a 3-4-3, with Bart Verbruggen selected in goal ahead of Kinski, although that goalkeeper call is acknowledged as a difficult weekly decision until David Raya can be bought on wildcard. Bryan Mbeumo starts at home to Manchester City ahead of Brighton’s Gomez away at Coventry: Manchester City’s defence has looked vulnerable, while Mbeumo continues to show goal threat. Joao Pedro is vice-captain behind Palmer.

Hull have kept three clean sheets but have conceded more than 5.0 xG, strengthening the case for targeting them with Palmer.

Bart Verbruggen starts over Kinski in goal, though the position remains unsettled ahead of a planned wildcard for David Raya.

items.headline: Cole Palmer captaincy drives Bruno Fernandes exit ahead of Gameweek 4
items.summary:
Gameweek 3 is a red-arrow week for both managers, with Mark’s late Free Hit proving a marginal loss. The chip is intended to load up on Manchester City while avoiding Arsenal v Chelsea, but City score only once against Coventry, the Wolves defensive double-up fails, and Collins goes off injured. Isak and captain Erling Haaland provide the main returns, but Mark’s original squad would have outscored the Free Hit by three points; adding a Haaland Triple Captain would have produced a further nine points. Still, the Free Hit gives him another week of information and restores Martin Odegaard, whom he may otherwise have sold.

For Gameweek 4, Mark has two free transfers, no money in the bank and a squad containing Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Odegaard, Dominik Szoboszlai, Haaland, Joao Pedro and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. His preferred route is Bruno Fernandes to Cole Palmer, making Palmer captain at home to Hull, plus Joe Rodon to Diego Kiper as a short-term defensive punt against Coventry. Rodon is injured, a non-playing asset and likely to lose value, while Kiper has immediate clean-sheet upside despite becoming less attractive when Mitoma returns. Mbeumo is more likely to stay: he continues to deliver returns and minutes, while selling Bruno funds Palmer without sacrificing Brentford coverage.

Palmer is favoured over Morgan Rogers primarily because of captaincy. Chelsea’s home match with Hull is the standout fixture, although Hull have opened with three clean sheets despite underlying numbers suggesting they have allowed enough chances to concede around five goals. Joao Pedro is also a viable captain, with around 70% ownership likely to make him the popular armband choice, but Palmer’s penalties and lower ownership offer more upside. Fernandes remains a dangerous sell, particularly after his recent hat-trick and with Manchester City visiting Old Trafford, but Palmer looks the cleaner premium captain and Bruno can return later if needed.

A Gameweek 5 Wildcard is increasingly likely for Mark. Newcastle, Everton and Nottingham Forest all gain appealing fixtures, creating entry points for Isak, Morgan Gibbs-White and Everton options such as Thierno Barry, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and James Tarkowski. Gibbs-White stands out as a secure 90-minute player on penalties and set pieces, while Fulham’s run of Ipswich, Hull and Coventry from Gameweeks 6-8 also puts Gonzalo Garcia on the watchlist. Arsenal remain essential defensively after allowing less than one expected goal across three matches, but budget options such as Odegaard, Solanke and Conor Kiwior make Bukayo Saka difficult to justify alongside Haaland and Palmer. The likely long-term captaincy core is Haaland and Palmer, with Haaland’s home games against Sunderland in Gameweek 5 and Ipswich in Gameweek 7 particularly attractive; Gameweek 7 is earmarked as a strong Triple Captain opportunity.
key_points: Transfer plan: sell injured Joe Rodon for Diego Kiper as a one-week Gameweek 4 punt against Coventry, then reassess on a likely Gameweek 5 Wildcard.
Cole Palmer is the preferred Gameweek 4 captain at home to Hull, with Bruno Fernandes the likely sacrifice to fund him.
Joao Pedro is a credible alternative captain because of his huge ownership and penalty-winning potential, but Palmer carries the stronger differential appeal.
Keep Bryan Mbeumo if possible: he is returning consistently, plays reliable minutes and does not need to be captainable to retain value.
Hull’s three clean sheets should not completely deter Chelsea investment, as Hull have conceded chances worth roughly five expected goals.
Martin Odegaard is a strong value Arsenal asset at £6.6m, while Arsenal’s elite defensive numbers support retaining two defensive routes where possible.
A Gameweek 5 Wildcard targets Newcastle, Everton and Nottingham Forest, with Morgan Gibbs-White, Isak and Everton’s budget options among the leading candidates.
Haaland remains central to the captaincy plan, especially at home to Sunderland in Gameweek 5 and Ipswich in Gameweek 7, the latter a potential Triple Captain week.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW4 ✅
items.headline: Palmer is the standout Gameweek 4 captain as Chelsea target Hull
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the leading Gameweek 4 captaincy pick, projected at 7.5 points for Chelsea’s home match against Hull, with João Pedro the strongest forward alternative at 6.4. Hull’s three clean sheets mask a defence that has conceded more than five expected goals and ranks only 13th for expected goals conceded, making Chelsea’s attack the week’s prime target. A move from Bruno Fernandes to Palmer is strongly favoured, while even selling Alexander Isak for João Pedro is considered worthwhile on both immediate and five-week projections. Palmer is also a serious Triple Captain option, although João Pedro is likely to be the more popular armband choice.

Arsenal’s defence remains the most reliable source of clean-sheet potential despite conceding early against Chelsea. They have allowed only 0.93 expected goals across three matches, and David Raya is the top projected goalkeeper for Sunderland at home. Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber offer excellent defensive routes, while Bukayo Saka remains a premium midfield option through penalty duty, corners and strong shot volume. Martin Ødegaard is an appealing £6.6m alternative after producing 1.6 expected goal involvement against Chelsea, though his minutes are still being managed.

For cheaper defenders, Digne is an attractive short-term Gameweek 4 buy for Coventry away but carries a post-international-break minutes risk. Luka Vušković is preferred as the longer-term option thanks to his set-piece goal threat and defensive-contribution potential. Ezri Konsa looks one of the best £4.4m picks after an outstanding Chelsea debut and could retain his place while Cibra is absent. Jan Paul van Hecke also offers value in a favourable Brighton run, while Palace’s Dassi is worth monitoring after playing 90 minutes against Fulham.

Managers should be cautious with early transfers because Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Palace, Hull, Sunderland, Manchester City, Newcastle, Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, Leeds and Manchester United all play in midweek before Gameweek 4. Early moves make most sense only to secure an important price rise. For Wildcard or Free Hit squads, the preferred strategy is aggressive team stacking: double Arsenal defence against Sunderland, double Brighton defence against Coventry, triple Chelsea attack against Hull and triple Liverpool attack against Fulham. A core of Erling Haaland, João Pedro and Whistler is favoured for a Wildcard, while Bournemouth assets are earmarked for Gameweek 7 when their fixtures improve.
key_points: Captain Palmer against Hull; João Pedro is the leading alternative and the likely template captain.
Palmer is a viable Triple Captain in Gameweek 4, but future Haaland and Bruno Fernandes opportunities make chip timing a trade-off.
Raya and Arsenal defenders are premium targets after Arsenal concede just 0.93 expected goals over the first three gameweeks.
Bruno Fernandes to Palmer is a recommended transfer, while Isak to João Pedro is also backed by short- and medium-term projections.
Konsa at £4.4m and Vušković as a longer-term pick stand out among value defenders; Digne is mainly a short-term punt.
Avoid unnecessary early transfers before a busy midweek programme unless a price change materially affects the move.
A Free Hit can justify double Arsenal and Brighton defence, triple Chelsea attack and triple Liverpool attack in Gameweek 4.
Bournemouth’s fixture swing from Gameweek 7 makes Tavernier and other Cherries assets future targets.

items.title: My FPL Wildcard Team for Gameweek 4 🔥 Triple Chelsea✅
items.headline: Saka and Haaland anchor Gameweek 4 wildcard despite Arsenal rotation concern
items.summary:
A Gameweek 4 wildcard is built around keeping Erling Haaland, Cole Palmer, Bukayo Saka and Joao Pedro, while targeting value in Arsenal and £5m-ish defenders rather than loading up on premium defence. Haaland remains worth holding despite Manchester City’s trip to Manchester United in Gameweek 4: he is the standout captain for Sunderland at home in Gameweek 5 and Ipswich at home in Gameweek 7. Joao Pedro is an automatic inclusion at £7.5m because of his secure minutes, lack of European football and home fixture against Hull, while Palmer remains Chelsea’s leading attacking target for the same Hull match and a favourable run thereafter.

Saka is preferred over a third Arsenal defensive asset, partly because of regret at overlooking him on an earlier wildcard. At around 11% ownership, he offers differential appeal, set pieces and penalties, and should start most league matches even if he features in the Champions League. Arsenal’s defensive picks still offer major value: Ezri Konsa at £4.4m is excellent, while Riccardo Calafiori has huge upside at his price after appearing dangerous against Chelsea. However, Calafiori’s Champions League involvement is crucial. If he starts in Europe, there is a greater fear he is rested against Sunderland; if he is benched, his Premier League prospects improve. In the former scenario, David Raya plus a £5m defender such as Van Hecke is a safer alternative.

The suggested defence uses rotating £4.5m goalkeepers Bart Verbruggen and Antonin Kinsky, alongside Konsa, Calafiori, a £5m defensive-contribution option such as Mavropanos, Lewis Hall and Neco Williams. Managers who dislike goalkeeper rotation can simply play Verbruggen with a £4m reserve. Hall, Jarrad Branthwaite-type budget options and Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi/Silva are alternatives, with Bournemouth’s fixtures improving from Gameweek 7. Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma replacement Kaiper is a higher-risk attacking defender/midfielder option while Mitoma remains sidelined, but his minutes may diminish once Mitoma returns.

In midfield, Morgan Rogers is retained despite a Chelsea triple-up with Palmer and Joao Pedro, as Hull are expected to regress defensively and Chelsea have the potential for a high-scoring win. Morgan Gibbs-White is the cleaner alternative, offering penalties and reliable 90-minute appearances. Pascal Gross at £5.5m remains a strong value starter because of his minutes and chance creation, with a cheap Hull midfielder such as Slater acting as the sacrifice bench slot. Dominik Szoboszlai is still a viable set-and-forget penalty option, but fitting him alongside Saka generally requires downgrades elsewhere.

The third forward is Yoane Wissa, whose fixtures—Leeds away, Hull at home and Coventry away—support patience despite a slow start. Everton’s Thierno Barry is the cheaper alternative: he is close to nailed as a £5.6m number nine, gets chances and may take penalties, although his medium-term fixtures worsen. Going without Haaland can fund Bruno Fernandes and a heavily upgraded midfield, but it creates difficult captaincy decisions in Gameweeks 5 and 7 and does not provide enough extra defensive value to justify the risk yet.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 5 against Sunderland at home and Gameweek 7 against Ipswich at home; his Manchester United away fixture in Gameweek 4 is still acceptable.
Prioritise Saka over triple Arsenal defence for his penalties, set pieces, low ownership and likely league minutes.
Monitor Calafiori in the Champions League: a start raises rotation concern for Sunderland, while a benching supports keeping him.
Use Raya plus Van Hecke or another £5m defender if Calafiori’s midweek minutes make him too risky.
Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro form an aggressive Chelsea attack triple-up for Hull at home in Gameweek 4.
Wissa is a strong third-forward hold for the next three fixtures, but Barry is a cheaper route to release funds.
Avoid a Haaland exit before Gameweek 7 unless the upgraded midfield outweighs losing the clearest captaincy option.
Bournemouth defenders, particularly Silva/Senesi-type options, become more attractive from Gameweek 7 as fixtures improve.

items.title: The PERFECT FPL Wildcard Team for GW4
items.headline: Gonzalo over Wissa anchors Dan’s Gameweek 4 Wildcard rebuild
items.summary:
Dan activates his Wildcard in Gameweek 4 to turn a collection of short-term punts, poor fixtures and uncertain starters into a durable squad intended to need no planned transfers until at least Gameweek 8. His previous side carries difficult runs for Manchester United and Sunderland defenders, unwanted Coventry assets from a Gameweek 2 Bench Boost, and unstable Manchester City midfield options such as Cherki. The objective is a “robust” 15-man squad with playable bench cover, allowing free transfers to accumulate for injuries, form shifts and the international break rather than being spent on fixture-driven repairs.

The first draft starts Kinsky in goal, with Spurs preferred to the other £4.5m keepers. Arsenal’s David Raya is viewed as the standout premium goalkeeper, but the gap between the remaining premium options and cheap starters is not considered worth the extra spend. Kinsky’s home fixtures against Everton, Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace are attractive, while Spurs are expected to become a stronger defence than Brighton, Bournemouth, Fulham or Hull. The defence contains Arsenal pair Calafiori and Concer, with Calafiori established as an attacking, first-choice left-back and Concer expected to cover the injured Saliba until at least December. Vuskovic and Maharovic are selected for defensive-contribution potential and aerial threat, while Lewis Hall offers Newcastle clean-sheet, set-piece and rotation value from the bench.

Cole Palmer, Bukayo Saka, Szoboszlai and Pascal Gross make up the midfield behind Erling Haaland and Joao Pedro. Palmer is the leading Gameweek 4 captain against Hull, supported by his form, penalties and greater set-piece responsibility. Saka’s strong minutes and potentially improved penalty access make him a premium Arsenal priority. Szoboszlai is preferred to Gakpo because Gakpo’s minutes may become less secure as Liverpool’s new options settle in, despite Gakpo’s recent returns; Szoboszlai’s underlying shooting numbers remain encouraging. Gross is a functional £5.5m enabler with penalties, corners and free-kicks, and can be benched for Arsenal.

The key forward call is Gonzalo over Wissa. Gonzalo has 11 shots and 1.45 non-penalty xG in three matches, plays 90 minutes and may inherit Fulham penalties. Although Liverpool are first up, Manchester United’s openness is seen as exploitable before Ipswich, Hull and Coventry provide a three-game promoted-team run. Wissa is rejected because Newcastle’s chance creation has been limited, he has dropped deep, and the returns of Oscela and Fernandez Pardo could threaten both his role and minutes. Tavernier currently fills the final midfield spot after Sangare is substituted at half-time and Garner suffers an injury, but Dan identifies the Bournemouth midfielder as the least secure selection despite his strong xG, near-DefCon output, set pieces and possible penalty involvement.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the preferred Gameweek 4 captain at home to Hull, with Haaland and Saka providing premium alternatives.
Kinsky is selected as a £4.5m goalkeeper because Spurs’ fixture run is strong and non-Raya premium keepers do not justify their price.
Calafiori and Concer form a double Arsenal defence, with Concer expected to benefit from Saliba’s long absence.
Vuskovic and Maharovic are long-term defensive picks for DefCon points, set-piece threat and the ability to return even without clean sheets.
Gonzalo is chosen over Wissa after strong early shot and xG numbers, secure 90-minute appearances and Fulham’s favourable run from Gameweek 5 onward.
Lewis Hall is a valuable rotation defender for Newcastle’s upcoming fixtures and is preferred to Livramento due to his stronger role and set-piece access.
Tavernier is the most tentative Wildcard pick; his attacking numbers and set pieces appeal, but he could be replaced before the deadline.
The squad is built to roll transfers after the Wildcard, potentially reaching five free transfers by Gameweek 8 rather than booking immediate moves.

items.title: My FPL GW4 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 4 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Palmer is the Gameweek 4 captain as Chelsea’s Hull fixture outweighs Haaland’s United appeal
items.summary:
Gameweek 3 produces an unusually low-scoring round for many popular FPL assets, with Haaland, Isak and Sesko the only forwards to score. Haaland’s nine-point return against Coventry is respectable but underwhelming for the many managers who use Triple Captain, while Isak punishes wildcard sellers with a goal against Ipswich. Mbeumo also returns immediately after being the most-sold player, while Bruno Fernandes, Foden, Cherki and Thiago blank. Thiago remains a sell despite 2.4 xG without a goal, as Brentford’s fixtures worsen from Gameweek 4.

The priority move for Gameweek 4 is Foden to Cole Palmer, with Palmer taking the captaincy at home to Hull and João Pedro vice-captain. Hull have somehow kept three consecutive clean sheets, but have conceded more than five expected goals and are unlikely to sustain that record against Chelsea. Haaland remains a strong alternative captain against Manchester United, particularly given his record in that fixture, but City’s attacking rotation makes most of their midfielders unattractive. Semenyo and Enzo are the safer City midfield considerations, while Anderson is viewed as their best long-term value option.

A wildcard side can plausibly go without Haaland in Gameweek 4 to accommodate Palmer, João Pedro and premium Arsenal options, although it is a high-risk call. Arsenal offer exceptional depth: Raya is a leading goalkeeper option, Gabriel and Calafiori carry set-piece and attacking appeal, Ødegaard has two double-digit returns in three matches at £6.6m, and Saka, Rice and Havertz all remain viable. Chelsea’s Palmer and João Pedro are considered holds rather than short-term punts, despite Arsenal beating Chelsea 2-1 in Gameweek 3.

The proposed Gameweek 4 XI is Raya; Van Hecke, De Cuyper and Konsa; Saka, Foden, Szoboszlai and Groß; Haaland, Wissa and João Pedro, with £3.3m deliberately held back to fund Foden to Palmer. Retaining budget after that switch preserves defensive flexibility: a fifth-defender slot is kept cheap with Mendy rather than spending on Djed Spence or Ajer, leaving funds to upgrade Konsa or De Cuyper to the stronger £5m-plus defender pool. Bournemouth defenders, particularly Silva, become targets from Gameweek 7 when their schedule improves, while De Cuyper can cover the short term before a potential switch.
key_points: Transfer Foden to Cole Palmer for Gameweek 4 and captain Palmer at home to Hull; João Pedro is the preferred vice-captain.
Haaland is still a credible captain against Manchester United, but nine points from his Coventry match is only a middling Triple Captain outcome.
Avoid most Manchester City attackers because of rotation risk, with Anderson the standout longer-term midfield value and Semenyo or Enzo safer alternatives.
Ødegaard is emerging as a £6.6m Arsenal bargain after two double-digit returns in his first three matches, while Raya, Gabriel, Calafiori, Saka and Havertz offer competing Arsenal routes.
Sell Thiago despite his underlying 2.4 xG, as Brentford move into Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool fixtures.
Djed Spence has significant attacking upside but carries longer-term selection and defensive risk, with Livramento having already been benched.
Target Bournemouth defenders from Gameweek 7, when Sunderland at home begins a favourable run; Silva is a leading £5m option.
Keep cash in reserve rather than over-investing in a fifth defender, as the £5m-plus defensive bracket offers far better replacement options than the £4.5m tier.

items.title: 3x TRANSFERS CONFIRMED! OR WILDCARD? ♻️ MY FPL GW4 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Palmer and Gibbs-White moves allow Gameweek 6 Wildcard wait
items.summary:
Three transfers are already confirmed for Gameweek 4: Bruno Fernandes makes way for Cole Palmer ahead of Chelsea’s home match with Hull, Solanke is upgraded to Morgan Gibbs-White, and Rodon is sold for Muharemovic. Palmer is preferred despite Hull’s clean-sheet start because their underlying defensive numbers remain poor and Chelsea are creating chances; Gibbs-White appeals as Nottingham Forest’s set-piece and penalty taker, as well as their main open-play threat, for Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace. Muharemovic is chosen partly to avoid Rodon’s price fall and offers DefCon and attacking appeal against Newcastle and Crystal Palace, although Ben White and Ezri Konsa were considered.

The current squad is viewed as strong enough to avoid an immediate chip. Verbruggen is marginally preferred over Kinsky in goal, away at Coventry rather than at home to Everton, while the key outfield dilemma is whether to start Brighton’s Gomez at Coventry or Bryan Mbeumo against Manchester City. Gomez has the fixture and a full midweek rest, but Mbeumo’s quality and City’s tendency to concede chances make him difficult to bench. Szoboszlai is a concern because of limited attacking output and occasional right-back minutes, but Fulham at home keeps him in the side for now. João Pedro, Calvert-Lewin and Erling Haaland lead the line, with either João Pedro or Palmer set to be captain.

European fixtures raise fresh rotation and injury risks, with Aston Villa and Manchester City playing in the Champions League on Tuesday, Liverpool and Arsenal on Wednesday, and Manchester United on Thursday. That makes waiting on transfers advisable where possible. Palmer is the preferred short-term Chelsea midfield target for Hull at home because his penalties and explosive ceiling outweigh Morgan Rogers’ value appeal, while João Pedro is considered the standout Chelsea attacker overall. A Chelsea attacking triple-up is viable, especially with no European schedule, but two Chelsea attackers is the likely standard approach.

A Gameweek 4 Wildcard would feature Raya, Calafiori and Konsa in defence, plus Palmer, Gibbs-White, Pascal Gross and Mbeumo behind Wissa, João Pedro and Haaland. However, it may overcommit to lower-upside defenders and make a later move for Bukayo Saka or Martin Ødegaard awkward. A Free Hit would aggressively target Chelsea against Hull, Brighton at Coventry, Arsenal against Fulham and Liverpool against Sunderland, with options including Saka, Palmer, Rogers, Gakpo, Alexander Isak and João Pedro. For now, neither chip is planned: the squad projects well for both Gameweeks 4 and 5, allowing a transfer roll in Gameweek 5 and a planned Wildcard in Gameweek 6 over the international break. A significant midweek injury, mounting price-loss concerns or fear of missing Arsenal and Isak could still trigger a chip.
key_points: Cole Palmer, Morgan Gibbs-White and Muharemovic are the three confirmed transfers in for Gameweek 4, replacing Bruno Fernandes, Solanke and Rodon.
Captaincy is a close call between João Pedro and Palmer, with Palmer’s penalty role and haul potential strengthening his case against Hull.
Start Verbruggen over Kinsky is the current goalkeeper call, while Gomez versus Mbeumo is the main outfield benching decision.
João Pedro is rated the best Chelsea attacker, while Palmer is favoured over Morgan Rogers for the immediate Hull fixture because of his greater explosive upside.
European matches for Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United create rotation and injury risks, so late-week reassessment is important.
The preferred chip plan is to roll in Gameweek 5 and Wildcard in Gameweek 6; a midweek injury is the likeliest reason to bring that Wildcard forward.
A Free Hit would load up on Chelsea, Brighton, Arsenal and Liverpool assets, but it is currently considered unnecessary because the existing squad has strong Gameweek 4 and 5 coverage.

items.title: Transfer tonight 🤔 Cherki 👉 Rogers ✅ FPL Gameweek 4 Early Thoughts 🔥
items.headline: Morgan Rogers becomes the priority as Cherki’s Manchester City minutes look fragile
items.summary:
Morgan Rogers is the standout Gameweek 4 transfer target, with a move from Rayan Cherki to Rogers planned to exploit Chelsea’s home fixture against Hull and a favourable longer run. Rogers offers dependable starts and strong durability, while Cherki’s 65-minute outing underlines the risk of Manchester City’s crowded attack. Cherki starts ahead of Phil Foden in the No. 10 role, but with Semenyo, Iliman Ndiaye and eventually Doku competing for wide roles, neither Cherki nor Foden looks secure for 90 minutes. Foden is the clearer sell after being benched, although Champions League team news should be checked first; Cherki is a less urgent exit and can be held for Sunderland at home in Gameweek 5 if managers want to save a transfer.

The proposed squad move is Cherki to Rogers, despite the risk of Chelsea’s midweek Carabao Cup tie against Leeds. Rogers is close to a price rise, and the transfer creates a three-man Chelsea attack alongside Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro for Hull at home. The argument is simple: all three are individually strong picks with reliable league minutes and Chelsea’s fixtures remain attractive after Gameweek 4, including Brentford away, Bournemouth at home, Everton away and Manchester United at home. Erling Haaland remains the captaincy focus for Gameweeks 5 and 7, while Joao Pedro is also a premium Gameweek 4 option against Hull.

Manchester United midfielders Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are not forced sales despite facing Manchester City at home. Fernandes hits the bar against Everton and Mbeumo scores again, while both remain likely to play heavy minutes and have a solid run after Gameweek 4: Fulham away, Spurs at home, Leeds away and Bournemouth at home. However, moving Mbeumo to Rogers or Fernandes to Palmer is a reasonable higher-upside play, particularly for managers with a Wildcard available to reverse the decision later.

At the back, Nico O’Reilly’s warm-up injury requires patience rather than an immediate sale. If he is likely to return for Sunderland in Gameweek 5, benching him for Manchester United is viable, especially as a City clean sheet is not expected. If he is ruled out longer term, Josko Gvardiol at £5.6m gains appeal, although neither City defender is an urgent buy. Arsenal’s Kiwior is a stronger budget option at £4.4m while Mosquera is absent, with a probable run at right centre-back beside Gabriel. For other replacements, Van Hecke at £4.9m and Leeds’ Mahamovic are preferred value defenders, while Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk is less appealing given a difficult fixture stretch and uncertain clean sheets.

Hull’s three clean sheets should not deter investment in Chelsea attackers: they have conceded 4.86 expected goals across the opening three Gameweeks and remain a side to target. Elsewhere, Mameadu Sangari’s half-time withdrawal after a yellow card is frustrating but not enough to force a sale at £5.7m; owners can bench him or monitor his minutes, while non-owners should avoid buying before difficult fixtures against Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool. Nathan Collins’ calf injury could improve Ajer’s Brentford minutes, but Brentford defenders are not immediate targets because their next four fixtures are tough.
key_points: Transfer priority: move Rayan Cherki to Morgan Rogers for Gameweek 4 if chasing Chelsea’s Hull fixture and Rogers’ expected price rise.
Sell Phil Foden more readily than Cherki, as Foden’s benching makes his starts uncertain; wait for Manchester City’s Champions League news before acting.
Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweeks 5 and 7, while Joao Pedro is a strong Gameweek 4 play against Hull.
Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are safe holds despite Manchester City, but Fernandes to Cole Palmer or Mbeumo to Rogers is a valid upside move.
Do not rush to sell injured Nico O’Reilly unless he is ruled out for several weeks; benching him in Gameweek 4 and reassessing for Sunderland is viable.
Arsenal’s Kiwior at £4.4m is a strong defensive value pick while Mosquera is unavailable, with a likely starting role through Gameweek 10.
Avoid buying Mameadu Sangari after his half-time substitution until his role is clearer, though existing owners need not panic-sell.
Continue targeting Hull with Chelsea attackers despite their early clean sheets, as their expected-goals-conceded numbers suggest defensive regression.

items.title: 72 POINTS SO FAR! 🚀 | FPL CHAI'S GW4 TEAM REVEAL! 🚨 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Cole Palmer becomes the priority as Foden’s City minutes undermine Chai’s Gameweek 4 plan
items.summary:
Chai sits on 72 points before Chelsea v Arsenal and Manchester United v Everton, boosted by a Triple Captain return from Erling Haaland and points from Liverpool trio Virgil van Dijk, Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexander Isak. His Gameweek 3 patience with double Tottenham defence also pays off, although Spurs are fortunate to keep a clean sheet against Nottingham Forest. Isak’s goal and early substitution are not a concern in isolation, but his Champions League workload ahead of Fulham at home needs monitoring.

The main Gameweek 4 priority is finding a route to Cole Palmer. Palmer looks central to Chelsea’s attack, plays with freedom, has secure minutes and offers a captaincy option for several weeks. Chai is unwilling to go without him even if Chelsea face Arsenal, and rates Palmer as a stronger medium-term pick than Bruno Fernandes. Managers with Bruno are advised to consider moving to Palmer regardless of Bruno’s result against Everton, with Fernandes still a viable future buy when Manchester United’s fixtures improve.

Chai’s own squad has two free transfers and £1m in the bank, but the clean route of Harry Maguire down to a cheap defender and Antoine Semenyo up to Palmer is not convincing. The available defenders around £4.5m-£4.9m, including Crystal Palace’s Chris Richards, Leeds options and Newcastle’s Dan Burn, do not appeal enough to justify the move. Selling bench midfielder Solace to fund Palmer would leave too weak a bench and could force starts for Joe Gomez against Arsenal or Maguire against Manchester City.

Phil Foden is the other major dilemma after another reduced role for Manchester City, with Rayan Cherki competing for attacking minutes. Chai is tempted to keep Foden for the Manchester derby because of his quality, history in the fixture and the possibility that his tactical discipline earns him a start, but accepts City midfielders are becoming difficult to trust. Semenyo appears the safest City attacker for minutes and remains dangerous despite being used wide at times. No transfer should be made early, however: Champions League fixtures for Liverpool, City, Arsenal and others could bring injuries, rotation clues and decisive information before the deadline.

Wildcard managers can reasonably target Gameweek 4, using the European matches to assess City and Arsenal selection. Chelsea’s attack is attractive enough to support a triple-up, while Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is favoured over Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez because Arsenal have the better clean-sheet outlook and Raya offers reliable long-term minutes. Morgan Gibbs-White is also endorsed as a secure, penalty-taking Forest differential, while Newcastle’s Johan Wissa is a buy rather than a trap at £6.2m given his likely penalties, minutes and upcoming Leeds away and Hull at home fixtures.
key_points: Prioritise Cole Palmer for Gameweek 4, with captaincy viable against Hull at home and in subsequent weeks.
Do not make early transfers before the Champions League programme, especially with Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal assets vulnerable to rotation or injury news.
Phil Foden is an increasingly risky hold because of competition from Rayan Cherki, although the Manchester derby gives him one final case to retain.
Alexander Isak remains a hold for Fulham at home unless Liverpool’s European line-up raises major concerns over his minutes.
Avoid forcing Maguire to a £4.5m defender solely to fund Palmer; the current budget-defender market lacks a standout short-term option.
Wildcard squads can favour David Raya and Morgan Gibbs-White over Emiliano Martinez and Bukayo Saka for security of minutes and long-term structure.
Johan Wissa is a recommended Newcastle forward at £6.2m, with penalties, likely 90-minute outings and favourable fixtures supporting the pick.
Cole Palmer is preferred to Bruno Fernandes as a premium midfield transfer, while Bruno can be revisited for Manchester United’s later fixture run.
